presentation.label: CALL AND RESPONSE
presentation.summary: Nordl3's call and response phrase generator on the audio tracks: call and response on one track, or a call on one and its answer on another.
presentation.overview: CALL & RESPONSE writes phrase pairs the way Nordl3's Call / Response Generator does. A motif of two to four steps is repeated and varied along the call by DENS and REPT, in the chosen scale; the response answers it with one of 31 strategies (echo it, answer upward, invert its contour, keep its rhythm and change its notes, resolve to the root, and more), pulled toward the call by TGHT, closed by END, mutated by MUT and transposed by TRNS. ROLE C+R plays call and response on one track, the generator's same output; ROLE CALL and ANS1-ANS8 split them over two tracks, each with its own sample. PHRS lays the phrases over the track length: C|R halves; CRCR, CCCR (three calls and an answer) and CCRR quarters, the repeated calls varied by VAR and the second response by MUT; or LAYR, call and answer at once on two tracks. Notes are trigs with PTCH locks, accents VOL locks; the stock sequencer plays them at the pattern's tempo, speed, length and swing.
highlights: Call and response on one track (C+R), or split over two tracks with their own samples
C|R, CRCR, CCCR, CCRR and layered phrase layouts; VAR varies the repeated calls
31 answer strategies and 11 endings from the generator, in eight scales
Real trigs and PTCH locks: edit any step as usual; no clock of its own
usage: Load a pitched sample on an audio track and choose CALLRESP in SRC SETUP's machine list: the track plays call and response (ROLE C+R).
The SRC page holds the call: MOTF, DENS, REPT, SCAL, PHRS and ROLE; SRC SETUP (a double tap on SRC) the response: ANSW, TGHT, END, MUT, TRNS and VAR. For three calls and an answer set PHRS to CCCR.

For call and answer on two samples set ROLE to CALL, then choose CALLRESP on a second track: it answers the first (ANS1) and holds the response's controls. YES draws a new call, or on an answer track a new answer.

controls.name: MOTF
controls.doc: The call's motif type, its rhythm and contour

controls.name: DENS
controls.doc: The call's density, how many steps sound (16 is the generator's Medium)

controls.name: REPT
controls.doc: Repetition of the motif along the call (23 is the generator's Repetitive)

controls.name: PHRS
controls.doc: How the phrases share the track length: C|R halves; CRCR, CCCR and CCRR quarters; LAYR both at once on two tracks

controls.name: ROLE
controls.doc: C+R plays call and response on this track; CALL the calls only; ANS1-ANS8 the answer to the call on track 1-8

controls.name: ANSW
controls.doc: The answer strategy (31 of the generator's); SRC SETUP on a C+R track, SRC on an answer track

controls.name: TGHT
controls.doc: How close the response stays to the call

controls.name: MUT
controls.doc: Mutation of the response (of the second one where there are two)

controls.name: VAR
controls.doc: Variation of the repeated calls (CRCR, CCCR, CCRR); SRC SETUP on C+R and call tracks

limitations: Needs the Modwerk base loaded over USB (beta) with the machine table (ot_machines). Card firmware cannot include it.

On two tracks, give both the same length (the pattern's normal length mode does) and keep them in one Part. An answer track whose call track is not a CALL & RESPONSE call or C+R track writes nothing. LAYR needs two tracks; on one it is C|R.
Pitch is a PTCH lock, -12..+12 semitones around the sample's own pitch: phrases above an octave fold back into it.
CALL & RESPONSE owns the trigs and the PTCH and VOL locks of the steps inside the track's length; other locks, trig conditions, micro-timing and swing stay.

The generator's styles, gate, tie and slide are not ported: its neutral style, medium register and motif accents are used, and the track's AMP envelope shapes the notes. DENS, REPT, TGHT, MUT and VAR run 0-31. The seed is kept but not shown on a page; YES advances it and shows it (on a C+R track it draws call and response together).
Not yet run on hardware or in the emulator.

storage.label: Storage
storage.conditions: From the USB package build.py makes from the sources (m68k-elf-gcc 16.2, -Os): 14,840 bytes of ColdFire code and data and 1,344 of bss (three phrases, a 64-step line and the page), one instance, 308 relocations, no stock-code sites. No DSP memory, no heap.

processing.label: CPU load
processing.conditions: Work happens on the UI task once per knob turn or YES: a phrase pair of up to 64 steps and an in-place rewrite of the track record, for the call track and each of its answer tracks. Nothing runs while the pattern plays.

impact.conditions: A knob turn or YES on a CALL & RESPONSE track; idle otherwise.

cpu.rationale: At most eight phrase pairs of 64 steps and record rewrites per edit on the UI task; nothing at interrupt level and nothing while playing.

dsp.rationale: No DSP code and no change to the DSP programs.

memory.rationale: 16,184 bytes of ColdFire code, data and state in DRAM (14,840 + 1,344 from the package header); the lines it writes are the tracks' own records.

tests.summary: Host checks only: the PHRS layouts; calls and responses are deterministic, inside their phrase slots and scale, and close on a sounding step; a C+R track is exactly its call track's calls and its answer track's responses; VAR varies only the repeated calls, MUT only the mutated response; the 31 strategies differ, endings close as the generator's, TGHT pulls the response toward the call; the semitone fold, the track-record writer and the settings packing are checked under the sanitizers; the package's machine record sits at the registry's index (test_engine.py). Not run on a unit or in the emulator.

license.declaration: The phrase rules follow Nordl3's Call / Response Generator (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Nordl3, Nordl3/Call-Response-Generator dbd1f0c35ecd37dd4d64747808fff7ea3629c1b6, index.html), ported to C. The Octatrack glue is original, in the shape of VECTOR's MIT native.c. No Elektron firmware, extracted routines, tables, samples or dumps are included.

access.location: Audio track: SRC SETUP's machine list (double-tap SRC), CALLRESP after the stock machines; its response controls on SRC SETUP
steps: Double-tap SRC, scroll to CALLRESP and press YES: the track plays call and response (C+R). The SRC page holds the call's controls, SRC SETUP the response's and VAR.
For two tracks, set ROLE to CALL and choose CALLRESP on a second track: it answers the first, with the response's controls on its SRC page and the sample's own SRC SETUP.
Push LEVEL on the SRC page for the stock sample controls and again to return; hold a trig for stock's page and its locks.
